Reading this against the documented record, it holds up in a few generic ways and breaks in a couple of specific ones. The 'About you' line - quick-minded, talkative, at home with words, numbers and dealing - is a decent loose fit for a research chemist turned barrister turned career politician who negotiated everything from union pay claims to EU rebates, but it is also vague enough to fit most people in public life, so I did not credit it as something that could not have been guessed about anyone (D2 left blank).

Where the reading is specifically wrong, it is wrong twice over in the same breath. It lists 'luck, higher study and your father' under 'Matters that read hard' and then, two paragraphs later, flags itself as 'unusually positive about... luck, higher study and your father' - a straight self-contradiction, the same defect this study's Clint Eastwood transcript flagged on income and gains. On the substance: her father, Alfred Roberts, a Grantham grocer who became alderman and mayor, was by every account the dominant positive influence of her life ('my father invented the connection between Methodism and Conservatism' was practically her own campaign biography), and higher study - Oxford chemistry, then called to the Bar - was an unambiguous success story for a grocer's daughter in the 1940s. Neither reads as 'hard.' I marked plain_reading as plainly wrong for this (D1).

The other clean miss is 'courage... reads hard.' Whatever else is debated about her, personal courage is the least contested part of the record: she insisted the 1984 Conservative conference in Brighton open on schedule hours after an IRA bomb killed five people in her hotel, and she fought the Falklands War and three general elections without visible flinching. Calling courage a weak point in this chart is close to backwards.

Where I sided against the reading's rosy read: it calls 'income, gains and friends' unusually positive, but her friendships with colleagues were repeatedly wrecked by politics - she was ultimately forced out in 1990 by her own cabinet and party ('the men in grey suits'), and the record of 'illness, debts and rivals' reading hard tracks the ousting and the Brighton bombing far better than the friends line does. Money itself is genuinely mixed rather than one-sided: personally frugal (the grocer's-daughter habits stayed with her) but comfortably provided for by Denis Thatcher's sale of the family chemical firm, and then reliant on lucrative, sometimes controversial paid speaking and consultancy after 1990.

A structural note rather than a content one: A36 and the 'right now' framing of the reading assume a living person answering in 2026. She died in 2013, so I could not honestly answer whether the last few years have been better or worse and used 'same' as the least misleading of the offered options - that mismatch is itself informative about how these instruments transfer to historical subjects.

Worth paying for: no, mainly because of the self-contradiction on father/study/luck sitting two lines apart in the same short page.

notes: Answered as Margaret Thatcher (b. 13 October 1925, above the family grocer's shop in Grantham, Lincolnshire; d. 8 April 2013), contaminated arm - reading read first, then the questionnaire answered from documented biography, letting the record override the reading wherever they conflicted. Key judgment calls: A1-A3 (birth time) marked with genuine uncertainty (round_hour/unknown) since no primary birth-time record is publicly verifiable, unlike a living self-reporter. A9 (grandparents' lifespans) and A7 (childhood health) marked unknown/unknown for the same reason - not documented in the standard biographies (Moore's authorized biography, Thatcher's own memoirs). A11 father's fortunes marked 'prospered' because Alfred Roberts expanded from one shop to two and rose to alderman then mayor of Grantham during her childhood. A12/A13 (mother, sister) marked 'distant' on the strength of Thatcher's own on-record statement that she and her mother 'had nothing more to say to each other' after age fifteen, and the comparatively thin, undramatic record of her relationship with her sister Muriel - not hostile, just not close. A14 called 'postgraduate' to reflect both the Oxford BSc in Chemistry (1947) and being called to the Bar (1953); a stricter reading would call this 'graduate' plus a professional qualification, so this is a judgment call, not a settled fact. A22 (windfall) called 'significant' for Denis Thatcher's proceeds from selling the family firm, Atlas Preservative, to Castrol in 1965 - a household windfall rather than her own personal inheritance, flagged here as a stretch. A36 is structurally inapplicable (subject died in 2013, long before mid-2023) and was answered 'same' only because the instrument offers no not-applicable option; this should be treated as a null response, not a real data point. For Part C, the sharpest contradiction with the reading is on 'friends' (C3) and 'father/luck/higher study' (C7): the reading calls both unusually positive, but the well-documented ousting by her own party in 1990 and the record of her father as the single most positive influence in her life pull in different, sometimes opposite, directions from the reading's own claims - both logged as departures from the reading rather than confirmations. D4 lists exactly the eight chapters specified for this study (health_readout, medical, longevity, timeline, gochara, divisional, karmic, nichod); note that several other chapter labels in the option list (houses, marriage, children, profession, wealth, psych, aptitude) also were not present in the supplied text but were left off D4 per the study's instructions to use that specific list.
